title: I put a trail camera in my backyard for a raccoon. Every night, the photos get closer to my house.
transcript:
I put a trail camera in my backyard for a raccoon. Every night, the photos get closer to my house. Something kept knocking over my trash cans, so I strapped a trail camera to the old oak at the back of my yard. It faces the fence. It takes one photo every hour, with a little flash.

The first night, I got nothing. Grass, fence, the dark line of the woods.

The second night, the photo at three in the morning was different. Same yard, but lower, like the camera had slid down the trunk. I went out and checked. It was right where I'd left it, strap tight.

The third night, the three o'clock photo showed my patio furniture. That's twenty feet from the oak, in the other direction. The camera faces the fence. It can't see my patio.

I buckled the strap so tight it bent the plastic.

The fourth night, the photo showed my back door, close enough to read the faded welcome mat. When I went outside that morning, the camera was on the tree, facing the fence. But the strap was on a different notch, and the lens was fogged on the inside, like it had been somewhere warm.

Tonight I couldn't sleep, so I went to my bedroom window and looked down at the oak.

I couldn't see the camera.

Then the flash went off.
